- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 2x recent peak or apply decay to next 5 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak), model often fails to anticipate; apply downward bias for 3–7 days post-peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply sentiment-weighted decay (e.g., 0.8x forecast if sentiment > 0.67).
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment to forecast adjustment.
- When true outcome is > 10x historical mean, model often fails to capture volatility; apply exponential decay to forecast for next 5 days.
